**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed)

The Agreement contains **no audit, inspection or verification right in Garman's favour**. Targeted searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "premises", "examine" and "access" surface nothing that would let Garman check our use of the Software:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use, p0029–p0037)** — the likely home for a usage-verification right — imposes only self-executing covenants (no copying, no reverse engineering, reasonable precautions) with no inspection or certification mechanic attached.
- **§ 20 (General Matters)** and the notice/boilerplate paragraphs (p0134–p0147) contain no audit provision.
- The only examination right in the document, **p0114**, runs *in our favour*: "Sparkling may itself or by retaining independent experts, examine and test the materials for compliance with the obligations of Garman hereunder" (source code escrow).

Because the rule constrains audits *against us*, the absence of any such right is better than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, Vendor's cost, no system access), and there is no unannounced-audit or remote-system-access exposure that would trigger walk-away. Accordingly I deliberately did **not** treat this as "missing" or propose limiting language — drafting in a capped audit right would hand Garman an entitlement it does not presently have.
